title: Investigate a cheap way to surface a stale marketplace clone to consumers
summary: Reusable lesson from OMARK-21's correction (2026-09-08): shipping a plugin release does not deliver it. A consumer's local 'opum' marketplace clone (~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/opum) is a separate cache with its own refresh step; nothing in the restart path reports that the cache is behind upstream dev, and sessions come up looking entirely healthy on the old build. This is the same shape as opum-agent's OPAG-56 finding that shipping a replacement hook is not rewiring a consumer. Investigate whether this repo can make a stale-clone consumer visible cheaply -- for example a documented pre-restart check consumers can run, a version marker a session hook could compare against installed plugin versions, or similar. The acceptable outcome includes 'no cheap mechanism exists, document the manual refresh step instead' -- the point is to record the finding either way, not to guarantee a build.
